topic: Can satellite orbital configurations optimize ML-based QoS by reducing propagation delays for latency-sensitive traffic classes?
consensus_response: Satellite orbital configurations can indeed optimize ML-based Quality of Service (QoS) by minimizing signal propagation time, which is critical for latency-sensitive traffic classes. By considering the unique characteristics of satellite links, including high fixed latency, advanced orbital configurations can reduce interference and maximize signal strength. A hybrid approach combining ML-based path prediction with advanced orbital configurations enables real-time monitoring and adaptation of satellite link conditions, ensuring optimal routing for latency-sensitive traffic classes. This optimization process minimizes propagation delays, thereby improving QoS in satellite networks.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the limitations of current QoS architectures in managing high fixed latencies on satellite links, emphasizing the need for a standardized way to gain link information required for path calculations and considering the impact of high fixed latency on path selection.
